_journey_note: MULTI-TURN JOURNEYS. A conversational capability cannot be proven by a single question: the whole claim is that turn N resolves against turn N-1. So every turn carries its OWN expectation, and the expectations are chosen to be UNSATISFIABLE WITHOUT CONTEXT — 'qual e a diferenca entre os dois?' cannot name L2 and L3 unless the prior turns were carried. That is what makes the context-drop mutation a real test rather than a formality.

_oracle_corrections.turns: source follow-up turns in J2-PT-PROFILES, J2-EN-PROFILES, J2-PT-SOURCE-INTEGRITY
_oracle_corrections.now: sources_continue_prior: the served `sources` must be non-empty AND every id must have appeared in the previous turn's sources
_oracle_corrections.why: Demonstrated defect in the oracle, not the engine. The source-evidence terminal puts the identities in the `sources` field and a lead sentence in the prose — that is the shipped contract, and the response genuinely carried ['GETTING-STARTED','ADR-001']. The probe read the prose, so it failed a turn that had done exactly the right thing. The replacement is STRICTER: a prose regex could be satisfied by the word 'spec' appearing anywhere, while this requires real ids that actually continue the previous turn's evidence.

`\w{20,}` demands twenty consecutive word characters with no space — a single twenty-letter word. Natural prose essentially never satisfies it, so the probe could not be met by any correct answer. It was written to mean 'a substantive answer' and expressed 'one very long word'. The replacement states the actual expectation: the follow-up must give a REASON tied to the readiness subject established in turn 1.

Same defect as O-2, and it hid a real engine bug: the declared capability is `ambiguous_clarification`, so an unresolvable reference must ASK, not decline as out of scope. The corrected probe asserts the clarification, which the engine currently fails — the correction makes the oracle harder to satisfy, not easier.

_oracle_corrections.was: 'O BANZA já pode operar dinheiro real?' / 'Can BANZA operate real money yet?'
_oracle_corrections.now: 'Em que fase do ciclo de vida está o BANZA?' / 'What lifecycle stage is BANZA at?'
_oracle_corrections.why: The paraphrase changed the SUBJECT and stopped probing its unit. Asked whether BANZA can operate real money, the engine answers — correctly and completely — that BANZA does not process payments at all; that is the payments boundary's question, not the lifecycle status. Demanding the string PRE-PRODUCTION from it was demanding the wrong answer. The replacement stays on the lifecycle subject the unit names, and the direct form was always passing.
